acceptance: The command accepts a file or a directory and returns the same findings as the MCP validate_results tool for the same input; a test compares the two.
Exit status is 0 when there is no FAIL, a distinct documented non-zero code on FAIL, and 1 on an unreadable input.
A JSON output option emits the findings in a documented shape.
The PR reports the WARN and FAIL counts from running the command over every bundle in results-data/bundles, as the evidence for a later decision on running it by default.
The command appears in help and the user docs, doc contracts are regenerated, and a changelog.d fragment is present.
context:
Origin: adversarial review of an agent-facing strategy for BenchBox, 2026-11-12. Owner decisions quoted here were made on that date. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Principle: anything the MCP server can do, the CLI can do, through the same core code.

Decision gate (before coding): check for an existing CLI entry that already wraps this validator or overlaps it (benchbox validate checks config files; benchbox results lists results) and extend it rather than adding a second command; run make duplicate-check-delta. If the corpus run shows FAIL on bundles the Explorer ranks, stop and report it as a separate defect instead of tuning the validator here.

Verification rubric: pass only if CLI and MCP findings are shown equal on the same inputs and the corpus counts are reported.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items are delivered together on one feature branch and one PR, as their umbrella item names (site work: BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site); squash-merged. Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Review note (2026-11-13): reporting host load as an INFO finding belongs to bundle-record-host-load-20261113, not to this item.

Revision (2026-11-13), after an independent critique and owner decisions: an earlier draft said the validator was reachable only through MCP; the repository script already wraps it. Reuse it; do not write a second wrapper.
description:
Problem: ResultIntegrityValidator (benchbox/core/results/integrity_validator.py) is reachable from the MCP tool validate_results and from a repository script, _project/scripts/validate_results.py (with --json and --fail-on-warn), but not from the installed CLI. A user, a script or an agent with only the package cannot run it.

Outcome: promote the existing script's behaviour into a CLI command that validates one bundle or a directory, prints PASS, INFO, WARN and FAIL findings, offers JSON output and a fail-on-warning option, and exits with the documented code on FAIL. The repository script then calls the same code instead of keeping a second implementation.

Non-goals: running the validator automatically at the end of benchbox run.
